transcript:
Header: Date/Time: 2026-08-11 15:00 UTC; Duration: 49 minutes; Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Riley Chen (Redwood SE), Maya Lopez (Head of ML, Apex Insights), Daniel Park (Infra Lead), Priya Nair (CTO)

Summary: Intro discovery focused on cost/unit economics for conversational agent and embedding use cases. Customer budget constraint ~ $10k/mo initial, target latency p95 < 200ms for short chats, evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for data residency and cost predictability.

Topics: per-token pricing, batching & KV caching savings, quantization tradeoffs, Dedicated reserved pricing, Private deployment overhead (networking/KMS/SOC2), benchmark plan.

Transcript: 
[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate the time. quick intros from our side, I'm Samir, I'm the AE on this account, and Riley is our solutions engineer.
[00:10] Maya: Hi, Maya here, head of ML at Apex. Daniel and Priya are with me.
[00:15] Priya: Hey all.
[00:20] Riley: Thanks. high level today we want to understand your workload and economics, so we can recommend Hosted, Dedicated or Private and a TCO. feel free to interrupt.
[01:02] Maya: Sure. brief context — we're building a customer support conversational assistant and a separate semantic search / reranking pipeline. expected 1.2M interactions a month initially, each chat avg 400 tokens total, embeddings for search are 768-dim vectors done at indexing time, maybe 50k documents to start. budget is roughly $10k per month cap for the pilot.
[01:35] Samir: Great, that's helpful. when you say 400 tokens total per interaction, is that input+output or just response?
[01:42] Maya: That's total. input prompts are short, maybe 80 tokens, outputs ~320.
[02:01] Riley: Good. we typically calculate cost per 1M tokens. for Hosted, our baseline pricing for generation models is around $X per 1k tokens for input and $Y per 1k tokens for output — I'm going to translate that to per million in a sec with an example. also, batching, KV cache for multi-turn sessions and quantized model variants can materially reduce unit cost.
[02:36] Daniel: Can you give ballpark numbers? we need to know if Hosted can fit the $10k budget or if we need Dedicated.
[02:45] Samir: Absolutely. quick example: if you do 1.2M interactions * 400 tokens = 480M tokens per month. at rough Hosted generation pricing, say $8 per 1M tokens (this is illustrative), that puts token cost at about $3.8k per month — but that's a naive calc not accounting for model size, output/input split, or embeddings.
[03:20] Maya: Wait so 480M tokens -> $3.8k? that seems low compared to our expectations. can you show the math?
[03:30] Samir: Sure. 480M tokens / 1M * $8 = $3,840. but important caveats: if you use larger context windows or low-temp higher token outputs, or a higher-priced model, it goes up. Also embeddings are charged differently — embedding calls for 50k docs at indexing time is a one-time cost per update.
[04:05] Riley: Also bursts matter. if you have many concurrent chats, latency SLOs at p95 <200ms push you towards Dedicated or higher-priority capacity which increases committed spend. Dedicated is reserved capacity — you pay a commit (monthly/annual) for predictable throughput and better p95. Example: Dedicated line might be priced equivalent to X GPUs monthly; for many customers that's $Zk/mo depending on model and quantization.
[04:44] Daniel: We are latency sensitive. 200ms p95 for short chats is sort of our SLA. can Hosted meet that?
[04:52] Riley: Hosted can meet <200ms p95 for smaller models and short contexts in many regions; for consistent p95 at peak we recommend Dedicated or a hybrid — route most traffic to Hosted and critical customer sessions to Dedicated or a pinned low-latency pool.
[05:20] Maya: Okay. what about batching? we heard batching reduces cost but increases latency. how does Redwood handle that?
[05:28] Riley: Good question. Redwood's runtime does continuous batching with latency-awareness. we set per-route latency SLOs; the runtime batches opportunistically within those SLOs. Typical savings vary: for high-throughput workloads with short sequences, batching can reduce per-token cost 20-60% depending on model & instance type. for your profile (many short chats) batching could save 30-40% on token compute.
[06:05] Priya: And KV cache — is that useful for our multi-turn?
[06:08] Riley: Yes. KV cache (sometimes transcribed as 'kay-vee cache' in older notes) caches transformer key/value states for a session so repeated tokens for the prompt or context don't re-compute. for chat sessions with repeated system prompts or user history, it can reduce compute by 10-50% depending on turn count.
[06:34] Maya: Good. What's the difference in ops between Dedicated vs Private? we have data residency and compliance needs; private deployment is attractive but we worry about overhead.
[06:44] Samir: Dedicated is still managed by Redwood in our data centers or cloud tenancy — you get reserved GPU pools with SLA and predictable throughput. Private is customer-managed control plane (VPC/on-prem) and gives you full network isolation and optionally air-gapped installs; it has a higher up-front integration cost and license, plus you handle some infra ops. For compliance-heavy customers Private or Dedicated in a customer VPC are common.
[07:12] Daniel: For Private, do we need to manage KMS/HSM?
[07:15] Riley: You can integrate your KMS/HSM. we support KMS integrations and can pass audit logs. That said, Private requires more coordination on networking, firewall rules, and sometimes on-prem hardware procurement.
[07:31] Maya: Are there SOC2 / ISO docs you can share?
[07:34] Samir: Yes, we'll share our SOC2 report and security whitepaper. action item for me.
[07:40] Priya: For Dedicated pricing, what does committed capacity look like? monthly GPU pool?
[07:46] Samir: Usually a commitment is via reserved capacity measured in vGPU units or throughput - e.g., a small Dedicated pool for Llama/opt-style models might start at $20k-$30k/mo depending on region and model, while medium enterprise pools are higher. I'll give you a concrete example in the pricing sheet tailored to your 480M tokens/month.
[08:15] Maya: That's above our $10k cap. any levers to hit our $10k target?
[08:20] Riley: Yes. a few levers: 1) smaller model family for majority of queries (cost delta is large), 2) aggressive quantization which could reduce GPU memory and hence cheaper instance types by ~30-50% cost reduction, 3) maximize batching and KV cache, 4) route only high-value sessions to Dedicated and rest to Hosted. We'll run a TCO scenario.
[08:48] Daniel: Can you quantify quantization? we worry about quality regressions.
[08:52] Riley: Quantization tradeoffs are model-specific. for many open models 4-bit or 8-bit quantization has minimal quality impact for typical assistant tasks. we recommend a validation eval on your prompt set. quant helps you run on cheaper GPUs or increase throughput per GPU. expected compute cost savings for quantized inference 30-50% in typical cases.
[09:20] Maya: What about embedding costs? those need to fit the budget too; we plan to embed 50k docs monthly when updating index, plus 10k incremental docs per month.
[09:29] Samir: Embeddings are priced differently - typically per 1k tokens of the embedding request or a flat per-call price depending on model. We'll include those numbers. rough ballpark: embedding 50k docs might be a one-off in the hundreds to low thousands depending on doc size and model.
[09:50] Priya: Is there a simple TCO example for us: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for our 480M tokens profile and 50k docs?
[09:58] Riley: We'll prepare a 3-scenario TCO with assumptions: model family (small-median-large), percent of traffic routed to Dedicated, caching/batching savings and quantization levels. Example top-line Hosted scenario: raw token cost $3.8k + embeddings and network + margin = ~ $5k-6k/month. Dedicated hybrid scenario with 20% routed to Dedicated and 80% Hosted might push to $9k-12k depending on commit. Private has a high initial license/integration (one-time) plus infra Opex. we'll send precise numbers.
[10:35] Maya: Your example earlier gave $3.8k hosted — when you add in higher-priced model variants and latency priority, that goes up. can you model worst-case vs best-case?
[10:45] Samir: yes. best-case (quantized mid-size model, high batching, KV cache) we might be in the $4k-6k range. worst-case (large model, low batching, low cache, high priority) could be $15k+. hence why we want to evaluate on actual prompts.
[11:12] Daniel: On benchmarking — what data do you need from us to run an apples-to-apples test?
[11:16] Riley: We'll need representative prompts, expected concurrency and traffic shape (RPS, peak minutes), and sample docs for embedding. Also success metrics: latency p95, cost per 1k tokens, and quality thresholds (BLEU-ish or human rating).
[11:34] Maya: We'll share that.
[11:38] Priya: Any constraints for running a quick pilot? networking? firewall rules?
[11:43] Samir: For Hosted, none beyond allowing API egress to our endpoints. For Dedicated/Private we need IPs, VPN/VPC peering or direct connect options, and potentially opening certain ports for health checks; Riley will share a checklist.
[12:05] Riley: I'll attach a network checklist and recommended instance types.
[12:09] Maya: Great. For quality, we want to ensure quantized models don't regress on our top 50 prompts — can we run A/B tests?
[12:17] Riley: Yes we support A/B rollouts and can do canary comparisons via our rollout tooling and evaluation hooks; we can capture quality deltas on your prompt set and tie alerts to regressions.
[12:34] Maya: Any limits or quotas on Hosted while we pilot? we don't want surprises.
[12:39] Samir: We'll provision eval quotas and set hard spend caps for your account during pilot. you control quotas and can opt into burst.
[12:49] Daniel: On the security front, do you support enterprise SSO / SAML?
[12:54] Riley: Yes, SSO via SAML / OIDC, RBAC, audit logs, and we can export token-level usage for cost analysis.
[13:10] Priya: For Private deployment, what's the expected timeline?
[13:14] Samir: Private deployments tend to take 6-10 weeks depending on integration complexity; Dedicated can be faster, often 2-4 weeks if capacity is available. Hosted is immediate.
[13:27] Maya: Okay timeline works. we have a pilot window in September.
[13:32] Samir: Perfect. we'll align the benchmark and a pilot plan to fit that.
[13:38] Maya: Quick question on fallback strategies — if Dedicated capacity is saturated do you route to hosted?
[13:44] Riley: Yes we can set fallback policies to send traffic to compatible model variants in Hosted or lower-tier Dedicated pools to avoid outages. that is built into our routing stack.
[13:55] Daniel: Any notes on regional pricing differences? we may host EU data in eu-west.
[14:00] Samir: There can be regional price deltas; we'll include region-specific pricing in the deck.
[14:12] Maya: How do you measure batching efficiency? like what metric?
[14:16] Riley: We measure GPU utilization, tokens/sec, and tokens per dollar; batching efficiency reflects average tokens per kernel invocation. We'll provide historical charts from similar customers.
[14:32] Priya: For embeddings, what about vector dimension and downstream index cost? are those external?
[14:37] Riley: Redwood charges for embedding compute and storage; indexing/search infra is typically your vector DB or a managed integration (we integrate with several). we'll surface both compute and storage line items in the TCO.
[14:57] Maya: One more on debugging — if we see a spike in latency, what's the escalation path?
[15:02] Samir: Our Dedicated customers get a named CSM and 24x7 support at higher tiers; for Hosted we have SLAs and dedicated channels for enterprise. we'll map that in the proposal.
[15:18] Riley: I'll note support tiers and response times in the doc.
[15:24] Maya: Good.
[15:28] (brief cross talk)
[15:50] Riley: to recap, we'll prepare: detailed pricing sheet + 3-scenario TCO (Hosted only, Hybrid Dedicated, Private), benchmark plan, network checklist, and SOC2/security docs.
[16:01] Priya: That covers what we need.
[16:05] Samir: Next meeting proposed — technical deep dive week of 8/24. does that work for everyone?
[16:12] Maya: Yes.
[16:15] Daniel: Works.
[16:17] Priya: OK.
[16:20] Samir: Great. action items will be in the follow-up. thanks, everyone.
[16:30] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcription: occasional label swaps and filler words omitted, some product names transcribed differently (e.g., 'kay-vee' for KV).
